items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: We knew about George Van Eps and we know about Allan Reuss, all the guys who knew how to play rhythm like that.

ctx.x: Wow. That’s being serious about your work.

Oh definitely. We knew about George Van Eps and we know about Allan Reuss, all the guys who knew how to play rhythm like that. But they were doing like studio work and recordings, freelancing in Hollywood in those days, with Paul Weston and all those Sinatra records. Great rhythm sections.
In the book that I was reading about you there is a short bit about a fire on your bus.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I went to Manny’s Music Store on 48th Street and bought a seven string Gretsch after I heard George Van Eps play it the night before in a night club.

ctx.x: Was it a big adjustment at first?

It was. I was doing a lot of studio work and in the evenings I was doing The Tonight Show. And I went to Manny’s Music Store on 48th Street and bought a seven string Gretsch after I heard George Van Eps play it the night before in a night club. And I think about five or six guitar players in New York City all bought them the same day.
He made a big impression then. Is it always the lower string that’s added — on the seven string?
